newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian shares seen drifting lower.
newsitem.headline: Indian shares seen drifting lower.

text.p: Soured expectations will drive Indian stocks down this week but brokers and analysts expect fresh demand to emerge at lower levels.
"I think the market could lose 150-200 points," said M.R. Madhavan, market strategist at ICICI Securities and Finance Company Ltd (I-Sec).

The benchmark Bombay Stock Exchange's top-30 index fell 127.58 points, or 3.63 percent, to 3,382.47 on Friday -- losing 53.15 points or 1.55 percent in the week -- after the government dashed hopes of promised incentives.
"There was a goof-up," said Sundar Iyer, a member-broker at the BSE. "It has demoralised the investing public."

The roller-coaster rally in January was singularly boosted by Prime Minister H.D. Deve Gowda who promised to unveil a series of market-friendly policy initiatives, but those hopes were dashed when the proposals turned out to be patchy.
"At stake is the question of faith and trust," said Sanjay Athalye, associate vice president (investments) at Tata Asset Management Ltd.
"It was a big let-down," said Sanat Dalal, a top member-broker at the BSE.
"The market has no reason to hold on," said Iyer. "I definitely see it yielding ground."

Contango (or interest) rates on carry-forward positions from one weekly settlement to the next rose to 27-30 percent on Saturday against 24 percent a week ago, traders said adding this indicated the market was overbought.
"I'll be surprised if you don't see unwinding of positions," said Paresh Choksey, a dealer at brokerage Chatturbhuj Enterprise. "The market will be subdued."
A fall in prices would lure fresh buyers, analysts said.
"I see huge support at 3,200-3,250 levels," I-Sec's Madhavan said. "Many funds had missed out on the earlier rally. They will come in strongly."
The BSE index had soared 24 percent to an intraday peak of 3,812.31 on January 16 before profit-takers cooled the rally.
Despite the dashed hopes Indian markets hold much promise for foreign investors.
"The best argument for the Indian market remains the one of earnings growth and price," said Jake van der Kamp at Hoare Govett (India) Securities Ltd in a January report.
"Among all the markets we cover only Pakistan is arguably cheaper and its political prospects and earnings growth are much more uncertain," he said.
Subra Subramanian, the firm's director of India research, said he expects the BSE index to rise to 4,000 this year.

"We believe that stocks with little risk to their cashflows and earnings will see a quick revival. Forex earners will benefit from the depreciating rupee. The only cyclical we favour is aluminium," he said in the report.
It advised investors to go for aluminium, banks, consumer non-durables, hotels, petroleum, pharmaceuticals, power utilities and equipment, software and telecom.
